Mourning black bunting trimmed in ash-grey wolf-claw embroidery draped the full length of the wall-walk parapet, claws pointing downward in the heraldic grief position.
A rival faction's amber falcon-stooping pennant flying alongside the castle's own blue-and-silver stag banner atop the watchtower's dual-pole iron bracket, signaling fresh alliance.
Festival garlands of gilded iron leaves wreathing the spire-tips above silver-on-purple star-burst pennants celebrating the heir's investiture week across the full roofline.
Rust-red-and-bone-white vertical livery columns painted the curtain wall's full height, each column centered with a stamped black bear-passant medallion in raised plaster.
A massive crowned-eagle sigil burned in gold pigment across the great hall door's full twelve-foot span, each wing-tip touching its respective doorframe in hammered gilt.
Three allied factions' pennants crowding the barbican's iron spires — wolf-silver, chalice-gold, and serpent-green — each on a separate pole pressing against its neighbor.
Coronation laurels woven from hammered-copper ivy mounted above the portcullis frame, framing a freshly carved crown-and-sword relief in pale cream limestone below.
Pearl-and-sable heraldic shield panels set into the curtain wall at fifty-foot intervals, each displaying a coiled-serpent sigil in raised iron relief against the dressed stone.
Sculpted heraldic bear statues flanking the main gate in charcoal-grey granite, each statue's chest-shield painted house-crimson with a white star-burst inlaid in hammered brass.
Teal-and-white diagonal livery stripes running the keep's full southern face height, interrupted only by a painted black moon-sigil medallion at the wall's precise midpoint.
Carved crowned-wolf motif painted gold-on-azure in the main gate arch's keystone high relief, re-gilded each spring equinox with burnished gold-leaf applied that morning.
Amber-on-black triangular pennants lining the inner wall-walk's full run, each displaying a skeletal-hand sigil stitched in bone-white thread at the flag's center field.
Crimson banners bearing a silver stag-rampant sigil draped from iron rings across the great hall door's exterior facade, antler-tips sewn in copper thread spanning full cloth-width.
Pale-gold-on-deep-green square banners hung from every gatehouse window bracket, the twin-sword-crossed emblem stitched in metallic silver thread visible from a half-mile distant.
Rust-red-on-bone-white silver-axe emblem carved in high relief into the keep's southern cornerstone, axe-blade edge traced in hammered copper wire re-burnished each midsummer feast.

Diplomatic-summit flags of four rival houses ranked along the inner courtyard's flagpole row — gules lion-head, azure boar-charging, vert falcon-stooping, and or moon-and-star — each on a separate dressed-oak staff.
